Subject: FW: Centaur Health RFP — quick internal alignment (NIST/EU AI Act + eval plan)

Folks — forwarding Centaur's RFP. They are explicitly positioning this as clinical decision support (likely high-risk under EU AI Act). They want: NIST mapping, EU AI Act position, and a concrete eval/regression approach (they mentioned proof-of-concept).

Notes / suggested positioning (draft):
- EU AI Act: Treat Centaur's usage as high-risk (we don't independently classify, but we provide the technical documentation and a conformity-supporting package). We can offer: technical documentation (model card + training data summaries), risk assessment summary, conformity assessment artifacts (test harness, evaluation reports), and an operations playbook (monitoring, incident response, rollbacks). For customers who must perform a full notified-body conformity assessment, we will cooperate and provide artifact packages.

- NIST AI RMF mapping: We'll produce a concise mapping doc that ties Redwood runtime capabilities to RMF functions (e.g., Identify: model inventory & provenance; Protect: encryption-in-transit/at-rest, KMS integration; Detect: anomaly/detector metrics in the console; Respond: automated fallback + incident playbooks; Recover: configuration rollbacks + golden model promotion).

- Evaluation / regression approach (recommendation):
  * Hybrid regression harness: automated regression tests (unit & integration) + sampled human review.
  * Sampling matrix (attached as draft): stratify by clinical condition, demographic buckets, prosted input lengths, and edge-case flags (low-confidence and hallucination-prone patterns).
  * Baseline metrics: precision/recall for labeled tasks, calibration error, hallucination rate proxies, latency percentiles, and token-level divergence.
  * Drift triggers & mitigation: automated alerts on metric degradation (> X% from baseline for 3 consecutive sampling windows) -> canary rollback to previous model variant + incident triage.
  * Data lineage & record-keeping: per-request trace IDs, KV-cache provenance, and evaluation artifacts stored in customer-controlled S3/VPC with retention policy.

Action items / ownership:
- Jonas: please prepare a 1-page technical note describing the runtime observability hooks we can surface to Centaur (traces, per-token cost/latency, model provenance fields). Also call out quantization/variant considerations for private Dedicated deployments.
- Marissa: draft the governance Q&A responses and the EU AI Act positioning language (include recommended wording for their external regulatory filing).
- Mina: build out the sampling matrix and a short CSV we can attach (start with 5k samples per critical workflow; see attached draft).

Deadline: aiming to hand over the full Q&A packet and attachments by COB 2028-02-21 so Centaur can take to their committee.

Thanks — keep it pragmatic and minimize legal-speak unless asked.

—Kim

Ethan —

Appreciate the RFP and the clarity around the timeline. Attached is an executive preamble that summarizes our proposed deliverables and the high-level approach to NIST mapping, EU AI Act support, and our regression/eval plan. Highlights:
- We recommend treating the system as high-risk for the purposes of conformity documentation; Redwood will provide a conformity-support package (technical docs, evaluation reports, risk assessment) and will cooperate with third-party conformity assessments where required.
- Evaluation approach: hybrid regression harness (automated + sampled human review), an initial 5k-sample baseline per critical workflow, metric baselines and drift-trigger thresholds, and automated rollback policies for degradations.
- Deployment options: Hosted API for quick POC (synthetic data), Dedicated reserved pools or Private VPC for POC on customer data (we include KMS/HSM options and detailed audit logging).

Next steps:

2) If Centaur wants Redwood to run a POC on private data, we'll prepare a short SOW and a security annex.
